subject: Private deployment: network-aware patch window and cutover playbook
messages:
From: Jordan Park <infra-ops@acmehealth.com>
To: diego_fernandez@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Request: upcoming private patch - network cutover considerations

Diego / Marissa,

We need to schedule the May/June patch for our private deployment (VPC edge and on-prem transit) and want to surface network-level caveats before locking a window. Key asks from our side: 

- Confirm a 2-hour maintenance window where routing changes and VLAN maintenance can be applied (we prefer 02:00-04:00 PT, but flexible).
- Explicit rollback criteria for both model pinning and network cutover (how you want us to trigger network rollback vs app rollback).
- A short runbook for queue draining and KV cache invalidation during the cutover.

Attached is our current VPC topology for reference (acme_vpc_diagram.png).

We also have a compliance ask: our audit team needs a one-page summary of the rollback conditions and the timeline for any data-retention toggles during the window.

Can you send a proposed playbook and an owner list? We can include GreenBank SRE for cross-region routing if needed (cc'd Maya).

Thanks,
Jordan Park
Infrastructure Ops, AcmeHealth
attachments: acme_vpc_diagram.png (image)

From: diego_fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Park <infra-ops@acmehealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: upcoming private patch - network cutover considerations

Jordan — thanks for the diagram, that helps. Drafting a focused cutover playbook and ownership map; attaching v1.

High-level proposal: 

- Window: 2026-06-08 02:00-04:00 PT (proposed)
- Owners: Diego (cutover lead), Marissa (customer comms), Neha (rollback authority / safety gate)
- Preflight (T-72h): dry-run in staging, perf smoke tests, KV cache snapshot
- T-4h: final ticket/state sync, open NOC bridge, enable increased telemetry (10s token-level traces)
- T-15m: traffic rampdown to canary pool, freeze new deployments, drain existing KV caches using the KV-evict API (steps in playbook)
- Cutover: apply VLAN changes, commit config to transit routers, verify BGP flaps < 30s per AS path
- Post-cutover checks: 15/60/300s health checks, baseline latency comparison, token throughput sanity

Rollback criteria (network vs app):
- Network rollback: sustained packet loss > 3% for 2 consecutive minutes on primary path OR BGP convergence > 45s for critical prefixes
- App rollback (model pinning): quality regression on golden prompts > 10% or token error spike > 5% beyond baseline

If network rollback triggers, we will execute: 
1) Revert transit config (git rollback + apply)
2) Rehome customer traffic to previous edge via weighted routing (30 minutes to full)
3) Run KV cache integrity checks and rehydrate from snapshot if required

I attached diego_patch_playbook_v1.pdf — it's intentionally compact (4 pages) and lists commands, exact telemetry metrics to watch, plus handoff checklist. Two asks: please confirm the window (06/08) and give us final approval for Neha to be rollback authority.

— Diego
Diego Fernández
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
attachments: diego_patch_playbook_v1.pdf (pdf)

On Wed, May 20, 2026 at 11:05 AM diego_fernandez@redwood.com wrote:
> I attached diego_patch_playbook_v1.pdf — it's intentionally compact (4 pages) and lists commands...

Adding the network-runbook pieces — VLAN evacuation and quick-rollback commands. TL;DR: 

- Before VLAN change: run `show vlan brief` and snapshot with `vlan-snapshot save acme_20260608`
- Evac sequence: `evacuate-vlan <id> --drain-ports --retry 3` (this ramps endpoints to canary subnets)
- Fast rollback: `vlan-rollback <snapshot-id>` (should complete within 90s barring controller partition)
- Monitoring thresholds: if BGP peer reset count > 2 for critical peers within 60s, auto-trigger network rollback

I'll attach the quick commands file for ops (vlan-evac-commands.txt). Also recommend we add a brief pre-cutover BFD check between our transit and Acme's edge to avoid hidden convergence issues.

-Karthik
Network Lead, Redwood Inference
attachments: vlan-evac-commands.txt (text)
